intent: Add a non-coroutine epoll L4 forwarder with matching semantics, run a reproducible direct/coroutine/epoll A/B on d2, and document the value and cost of stackful coroutines.

findings.title: Transient accept errors terminate the forwarder
findings.why_it_matters: A failed inbound connection can make accept4() return ECONNABORTED or a pending TCP/IP network error. This branch converts every such error into app_fail(), stops the event loop, and closes all unrelated active sessions, so a remote client or ordinary transient network failure can turn one rejected connection into a full forwarding outage.
findings.suggested_fix: Classify ECONNABORTED and Linux's pending per-connection network errors (ENETDOWN, EPROTO, ENOPROTOOPT, EHOSTDOWN, ENONET, EHOSTUNREACH, EOPNOTSUPP, and ENETUNREACH) as rejected connections and continue accepting; handle ENOBUFS/ENOMEM with the existing bounded listener-retry mechanism instead of terminating. Apply the same classification to the coroutine sibling to preserve the shared contract, and add an injected-accept-error test proving established sessions and listener service survive.
evidence: learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/examples/l4_forwarder_epoll.c:1015-1016: `app_fail(app, negative_errno());` followed by `return;` makes every unclassified accept4() error process-fatal.

learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/examples/l4_forwarder_epoll.c:996-1013 handles only EINTR, EAGAIN/EWOULDBLOCK, and EMFILE/ENFILE before reaching the fatal branch; ECONNABORTED and Linux pending network errors are not handled.
learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/README.md:90-94 says a single-connection reset or I/O error must close only that connection, while infrastructure failure alone terminates the process.

Linux accept(2) documents that accept4() can return ECONNABORTED and can surface pending TCP/IP errors such as ENETDOWN, EPROTO, EHOSTUNREACH, and ENETUNREACH, which reliable servers should treat like EAGAIN.

findings.title: Capacity saturation leaves clients hanging
findings.why_it_matters: When active connections reach the configured cap, the epoll implementation stops arming and accepting from the listener. TCP handshakes can still complete into the kernel accept queue, so later clients appear connected but receive no service until an existing connection closes. If the active connections are long-lived or are themselves waiting on upstream connect deadlines, queued clients can wait for multiples of that deadline instead of being rejected as the documented and coroutine-forwarder semantics require.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the listener eligible while saturated, accept a bounded number of queued sockets, close and count them as rejected when active_connections is at the cap, and apply the existing short listener retry deadline to avoid a busy loop. Add a max_connections=1 parity test that holds the first connection open and requires the second client to be closed promptly by both forwarders.
evidence: learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/examples/l4_forwarder_epoll.c:991-993 also makes active_connections < max_connections a precondition for accept4(), so the saturated path cannot accept and close a queued socket.

learning/studies/20260910-stackful-coroutine/demo/examples/l4_forwarder.c:640-648 accepts the next socket, increments rejected, closes it, and backs off when the same cap is reached; the two advertised baselines therefore expose different overload behavior.

findings.title: Shutdown regressions can hang or pass benchmark
findings.why_it_matters: The A/B harness now certifies both forwarders, but its shutdown check has two green-while-red paths. A forwarder that leaks a connection can hit the one-second grace deadline, print forced_shutdown=true, exit zero, and have the sample accepted. A forwarder whose signalfd path stops consuming SIGTERM blocks the unbounded wait forever instead of causing the promised failed run. Either path prevents the harness from reliably validating the shutdown semantics it is used as evidence for.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the bare TERM/wait sequence with a bounded wait that escalates to KILL and fails the sample on timeout, then parse exactly one terminal summary from proxy_log and require forced_shutdown=false for normal benchmark completion. Make the normal phase of l4_e2e.py assert the same condition; retain forced_shutdown=true only in its dedicated forced-drain phase.

findings.title: Fixed order confounds the throughput comparison
findings.why_it_matters: Every round runs direct, coroutine, then epoll, so implementation is perfectly correlated with elapsed time. The captured host cannot expose or control its frequency policy, while the reported coroutine/epoll difference is only about 0.4%; warm-up, thermal, or shared-host drift can therefore dominate the comparison and make the parity conclusion non-reproducible.
findings.suggested_fix: Counterbalance the order across runs (for example, rotate all three modes or alternate coroutine/epoll order), record the actual order in the output, and regenerate the evidence before retaining the sub-percent comparison.

findings.title: Unrecorded RLIMIT controls epoll memory evidence
findings.why_it_matters: The epoll baseline allocates one watch entry for every descriptor allowed by RLIMIT_NOFILE rather than for descriptors actually used by max_connections. The same binary and benchmark arguments can therefore reserve radically different virtual memory, or fail startup under a tight address-space limit, solely because the host file-descriptor limit differs. Since the benchmark does not record that limit, its VmPeak comparison is not reproducible and can incorrectly attribute the observed gap to coroutine stacks.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a lazy chunked watch table keyed by fd, matching the runtime's existing 256-entry chunk strategy, so allocation follows descriptors actually observed. Also record soft and hard RLIMIT_NOFILE values in environment.txt and add a high-RLIMIT, low-max-connections startup/resource test.

findings.title: Generated evidence path violates repository confinement
findings.why_it_matters: The active evidence contract specifies an absolute machine-specific generation path, while the benchmark harness accepts that destination without rejecting absolute paths, `..`, repository root, maintained-output overlap, or symlink escape. A run can therefore overwrite maintained files or write outside the repository, and the promoted evidence lacks the required auditable path/digest manifest.
findings.suggested_fix: Express the clean root as a normalized repository-relative path such as `.tmp/rco-ab/final-evidence`; before any write in `l4_bench.sh`, resolve the repository root and reject absolute paths, `..`, the repository root, symlink escapes, and overlap with maintained or declared tracked outputs. Declare the exact promotable outputs and emit a path/SHA-256 manifest after successful generation, then add negative tests for each rejected destination.

triage_groups.title: Forwarder overload and failure semantics
triage_groups.context: The epoll baseline must preserve established sessions and expose reproducible memory bounds.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Fix transient accept classification and cap rejection first, then make watch allocation independent of RLIMIT.
triage_groups.why: These changes define whether the baseline is production-safe and whether its memory comparison is valid.

triage_groups.title: Benchmark false-pass controls
triage_groups.context: The evidence harness can hang, accept forced shutdown, correlate mode with time, or promote unconstrained outputs.
triage_groups.preferred_resolution: Bound child lifetimes, reject forced shutdown, rotate mode order, then regenerate a manifested evidence set.
triage_groups.why: All reported performance conclusions depend on the harness failing closed.

residual_risks: Established TCP sessions intentionally have no application idle timeout; production admission policy remains external.
PMU and CPU frequency controls are unavailable in the d2 KVM, so only affinity plus wall-time evidence is available.
testing_gaps: No stale queued epoll-event injection test.
No benchmark fault-injection test for malformed or zero-progress iperf JSON.
